- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤ 0.1) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates the drop; add 1–3% downward bias for 5–10 days.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is low; apply 3–5% downward adjustment for first 7 days if sentiment < 0.1.
- Mean reversion bias: if 10-day average of true prices is below forecast, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment spikes to 1.0 (e.g., strong bullish signal), model often overreacts; cap forecast at 5–10% below 30-day high for 3–7 days.
